sources.title: FAO species identification guide: Portunus trituberculatus diagnostic account
sources.scope: Ng1998 official FAO full-volume PDF: selected key figures21b/22b on printed1119 and species diagnosis/dorsal illustration on printed1125 were rendered and viewed. Three frontal teeth, four inner meral spines, nine lateral teeth/long last spine, granular broad shell and larger-chela basal conical tooth. Generic female abdominal diagram printed1047 is contextual, not a gazami specimen determination. No measurements/coordinates digitized.

retrieval.accessMethod: official publisher PDF download; selected pages rendered/read

sources.title: Naturalis — Crabs of Japan: Portunus trituberculatus
sources.scope: Institutional regional morphology account: granulated broad shell, regional ridges, inner/outer carpal spines and expanded final limbs. Its two-tooth/two-lobe frontal wording conflicts with the selected FAO three-tooth key; retained explicitly as unresolved, not silently equated or used to rename the species.

sources.title: JAMSTEC BISMaL — gazami taxon representation
sources.scope: Institutional taxonomic representation includes subgenus Portunus (Portunus); synonymous binomial is the same species accession, not an additional species. Recorded specimens/ranges are not independently inferred native boundaries.

decision: Substantial initial educational correction with partially working supported movement; not biological certification or a fully realistic measured model.

shape.before: Generic smooth beige oval, weak frontal region, thin rod-like limbs, two simple paddle tips and small local chela control.
shape.changed: A distinct broad roughened shell with regional eminence/ridge cues, nine marginal teeth on each side and long last spines, plus three frontal teeth using the selected FAO key. Thicker mottled chelipeds have four inner meral spine cues, inner/outer carpal cues, ridged cream/olive palms, dark curved fingers and a larger-chela basal conical-tooth cue. Six pointed walking legs differ from the expanded articulated P5 pair; paddle bases were filled to improve joint continuity.
shape.remaining: Unmeasured outline, tooth spacing, joint positions and limb ratios. Simplified mouthparts, underside, pleopods and gills. The selected dorsal caption labels a female; maturity and ventral identity are not independently determined. Naturalis uses two-tooth/two-lobe frontal wording; the difference is disclosed rather than silently equated with the FAO key.

surface.before: Nearly uniform tan material and coarse generic relief fail the selected olive, spotted, granular reference.
surface.changed: Original numerical olive/brown mottling, restrained pale spots, finer instanced granulation and cuticle normal field; dark/cream cheliped regions, blue-grey plated walking legs and dark finger/tip cues. Initial over-bright jagged flecking was reduced and the bare blue proximal chelae were corrected to darker mottled dorsal surfaces.
surface.remaining: Selected photograph is not calibrated live albedo or 3D material data. Spot placement, wetness, roughness, wear, setae and joint margins remain authored. The result still has simplified/stylized surface details and does not establish photoreal metrology.

movement.before: A local chela gesture on fixed generic limbs, without a grounded gait or articulated swimming mechanism.
movement.changed: Same meshes/materials across a supported short lateral walking bout, local chela/antennule gestures, quiet support and reset. Broadened P5 blades use a new reciprocating/feathering loop with both walking sets carried. Qualitative body-relative loop context comes from the biological section of Chen et al.2022.
movement.remaining: No raw tracked coordinates, biological joint axes/ranges, calibrated frequency, reaction force or fluid model. No predicted propulsion, prey capture, ingestion, sleep, growth or courtship. Robot servo limits and engineering validation are explicitly excluded from biological claims.

reviewMethod: Qualitative author comparison of60 actual final main-viewer WebGL2 states plus three views of one actual static GLB export on nine labelled sheets. Authentic Almandine source photograph and actually rendered selected FAO/Chen pages were compared. Existing253 records are unchanged. No independent specialist assessment, measured accuracy percentage or physiological simulation.

fao.viewed: PDFpages437/443, printed1119/1125, figures21b/22b and selected diagnosis/dorsal illustration; generic female abdomen on printed1047 from official chapter.
fao.scope: Full-volume download succeeded; only selected pages reviewed. Earlier NHM and split-part29 failures are retained in provenance. Figures linked, not redistributed.

chen.viewed: Actual PDFpages4/6, figures1/2 and4; selected biological sections2.1–2.4. Page7 robot schematic also inspected to distinguish engineering limits.
chen.scope: No digitized coordinate fit or reported sample size transferred to our model. No robot geometry, joint limits or performance are presented as animal measurements.

taxonomy.alternate: Portunus (Portunus) trituberculatus includes a subgenus, not a subspecies or second species accession.

names.scope: Gazami crab retained as a common-name variant; FAO uses Horse crab and EU commercial names vary. No Smithsonian collection determination was used.

fixesAfterFirstRender: Reduced excessive pale shell/chela/paddle flecks and softened pigment thresholds.
Replaced bare blue cheliped merus/carpus shading with selected dark spotted dorsal regions and pale undersides.
Narrowed initially round paddle blades, filled proximal paddle ends and added asymmetric terminal-blade contour for more continuous articulated surfaces.
Corrected primary-paper attribution to first author Chen after inspecting its bibliographic page.
Split screenshot collection into saved bounded batches after a browser-control execution timed out; final60 captures were completed and inspected.
